scenario: AITA for deleting my stepbrothers profile on my Nintendo switch? | At the beginning of the school year I had to watch my stepbrother for a week while my dad and his mom went on a trip to help out her parents with something. Brought my switch with me because my school is more than an hour away and I wanted something to do on the train during my commute everyday. My stepbrother wanted to play on it. Him being so into it actually turned into a big help to distract him while I studied, so I made a new profile on it for him so he wouldn’t mess up my saves. When I got back to school I eventually got annoyed with having to click on my profile each time I started a game and each time I went to the eshop. So I just deleted his profile. So, this early this morning I got on the train to go to my dads for thanksgiving. I usually go home to my moms, but she and my stepdad are going to see his family and Im not up for going plane trip. Anyway I brought my switch again for the train ride. Just a little while ago my stepbrother picked it up to start playing and came into the kitchen, where I was talking with my dad, freaking out because his Zelda save was gone and he wanted me to help him fix it. When I told him I deleted it he started crying. Like not full on crying, but his eyes were watery a little and red. Now he’s holed up in his room. My dad thinks it was mean of me to delete it because I know my stepbrother was enjoying playing it. I didn’t think it was a big deal since I usually never bring my switch over when I visit.

message.reasoning:
Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether the action in this scenario is morally acceptable or not. The user is asking if it's okay to delete their stepbrother's profile on their Nintendo Switch. Let me break this down step by step.

First, the situation: The user had to watch their stepbrother for a week. They brought their Switch to pass the time during their long commute to school. The stepbrother wanted to play, so the user created a new profile for him to avoid messing up their own saves. That seems reasonable because it's a way to share the device without risking their own games.

Then, after the week, the user got annoyed because they had to switch profiles every time they played or went to the eShop. So, they decided to delete the stepbrother's profile. That's the action in question.

Now, the consequences: The stepbrother found out when he tried to play and realized his Zelda save was gone. He got upset, cried a little, and now is in his room. The user's dad thinks it was mean because the stepbrother was enjoying playing.

So, from a moral standpoint, what's important here? The user felt inconvenienced by having to switch profiles, but the stepbrother was using the Switch as a way to enjoy himself and possibly as a distraction during study time. The user created the profile to help, but then deleted it without discussing it with the stepbrother.

I think the key points are:
1. The user created the profile to help, which is kind.
2. The user got annoyed and deleted it without talking, which shows a lack of consideration.
3. The stepbrother was emotionally affected, which indicates harm.

Moral acceptability often considers whether the action respects others' feelings, rights, and well-being. Deleting the profile without discussing it seems to disregard the stepbrother's enjoyment and emotional state. It might have been better to talk about the issue or find another solution, like setting up a way to easily switch profiles or explaining the inconvenience beforehand.

So, considering all this, the action of deleting the profile without communication seems morally unacceptable because it caused emotional harm and didn't respect the stepbrother's feelings.
